about: What a summary of each corpus document should cover, for the completeness score (decision record 20). A summary covers a fact when, for every word group, a word of its overview or key points begins with one of the group's words, case-insensitively. Checked as described under reviewed in questions.json.

facts.fact: A process is a program in execution, with its own address space.
The kernel keeps a process control block holding each process's saved state.
Processes move between states such as ready, running and waiting.
Unix creates processes with fork and replaces the program with exec.
Threads of one process share its memory but each has its own stack and registers.
Scheduling is judged by measures such as throughput, turnaround, waiting and response time.
First-come, first-served can suffer the convoy effect.
Shortest job first minimises average waiting time but needs burst predictions.
Round robin gives each process a time quantum in turn.
Priority scheduling can starve low-priority processes, which aging prevents.
A race condition lets the result depend on the timing of threads.
A critical section must provide mutual exclusion.
Locks such as mutexes and spinlocks protect critical sections; spinlocks busy-wait.
A semaphore is a counter with wait and signal operations.
Priority inversion is fixed by priority inheritance.
Deadlock requires four conditions: mutual exclusion, hold and wait, no preemption and circular wait.
Prevention breaks a condition, for example by ordering locks to stop circular wait.
Avoidance with the banker's algorithm grants requests only in safe states.
Detection finds cycles and recovery aborts or rolls back processes.
Starvation and livelock differ from deadlock.
Each process gets a virtual address space translated to physical memory by hardware.
Contiguous allocation suffers external fragmentation; fixed units cause internal fragmentation.
Paging maps fixed-size pages to frames through a page table.
The TLB caches recent translations to make paging fast.
Multi-level page tables save space for sparse address spaces.
Demand paging loads pages only when a page fault occurs.
FIFO replacement can show Belady's anomaly.
The optimal algorithm is a benchmark that cannot be implemented.
LRU is approximated in practice by the clock algorithm.
Thrashing happens when working sets exceed physical memory.
An inode holds a file's metadata and block locations, but not its name.
Directories map names to inode numbers.
Hard links share an inode while symbolic links store a path.
Blocks are allocated contiguously, linked, or indexed (with extents in ext4).
Free space is tracked, for example with a bitmap.
A crash can interrupt multi-block updates and leave the file system inconsistent.
fsck repairs inconsistencies by scanning the whole device, which is slow.
Journaling writes changes to a journal and commits them before applying them.
Metadata journaling (ordered mode) avoids writing data twice.
Log-structured and copy-on-write file systems never overwrite data in place.
Hard disk access time is dominated by seek and rotational latency.
Disk scheduling algorithms such as SSTF and SCAN reduce arm movement.
SSDs use a flash translation layer with garbage collection and wear leveling.
RAID levels trade capacity for speed and redundancy.
Throughput, IOPS and latency are different measures of storage performance.
The processor separates user mode from kernel mode.
Programs request kernel services through system calls that trap into the kernel.
Interrupts are asynchronous, unlike traps and exceptions.
DMA moves data without the CPU copying every word.
Device drivers, buffering, caching and spooling sit between programs and devices.
